translations.answer: Maintainers first trace back from aligned_free, finding that different Eigen vectorization/CPU compilation options were used in the same process. They recommend all dependencies use find_package(pinocchio REQUIRED) and pinocchio::pinocchio. The author found that removing -march=native in one library resolved the issue. Therefore, the main issue is cross-library ABI and compilation option consistency; it cannot be simply attributed to buildModel or URDF itself.
translations.applicability: Directly applicable to the original post Ubuntu Focal/Pinocchio 2.6.20/OCS2 mixed dependency build; other versions/platforms need to verify actual compilation commands and crash stack.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Maintainers provided two CMake write styles, both using find_package(pinocchio REQUIRED) and target_link_libraries(... pinocchio::pinocchio).
translations.details.attempts.1: The author removed -march=native from just one library.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compare all linked libraries' compilers, Eigen vectorization options, and -march options, not just URDF content.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Compare how each library accesses Pinocchio; the maintainer recommends using pinocchio::pinocchio imported target to propagate dependencies and compilation defines.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Ensure all Pinocchio/Eigen dependencies in the same process use compatible and consistent compilation options; removing -march=native in one library resolved the issue.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: CMake projects should prioritize linking pinocchio::pinocchio, and no longer manually concatenate Pinocchio/Eigen include, library, and compilation defines from different libraries.
translations.details.environments.0: Ubuntu Focal; Pinocchio 2.6.20 amd64; OCS2 getPinocchioInterfaceFromUrdfModel; two indirect dependencies use CMake package and pkg-config.
translations.details.limits.0: The original post does not provide a unified compilation after the build; cannot attribute all buildModel errors to -march=native.
translations.details.limits.1: The root cause is in-consistent compilation options within the same process, not -march=native in all projects.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author explicitly reports the segmentation fault disappeared after removing -march=native in library A; the maintainer adds that such mixed use is not unique to Pinocchio and closes the issue as completed.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: What should be checked first when a Pinocchio URDF buildModel call fails after adding another Pinocchio dependency library?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before deploying WBC on real hardware, run URDF loading and dynamics smoke tests on a build product matching the target CPU to avoid ABI issues during control process startup.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The maintainer points out that different vectorization compilation options lead to different malloc/free paths in Eigen; the author later finds that library A alone enabled -march=native.
translations.details.symptoms.0: crash during pinocchio::urdf::buildModel in Eigen aligned allocator free path; GDB backtrace into JointModelCompositeTpl destructor.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The function works in other examples, but fails only when both libraries that depend on Pinocchio are linked.
